lessons.title: The Pawn Wedge
lessons.story: A quiet Italian game develops naturally, but White's centre is slowly becoming more powerful. Watch how the pieces are placed as the position builds toward a tactical opportunity.
lessons.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Be7 4. d3 Nf6 5. O-O O-O 6. Re1 d6 7. c3 Be6 8. Bb3 h6 9. d4 exd4 10. cxd4 Re8

commentary.text: White begins with e4, taking space in the centre and opening lines for the queen and king-side bishop.
Black answers with e5, meeting White in the centre and keeping the position balanced.
The knight develops to f3, attacks the e5 pawn and prepares White to castle quickly.
Black develops the knight to c6, protects e5 and strengthens control of the central squares.
White's bishop comes to c4, becoming active and adding pressure toward Black's king side.
Black develops the bishop to e7, preparing to castle and keeping the position solid.
White supports the centre with d3 and opens a path for the dark-squared bishop.
Black brings the knight to f6, develops another piece and increases pressure on White's central pawn.
White castles, placing the king safely while bringing the rook closer to the centre.
Black also castles, completing king safety before the central tension begins to grow.
White places the rook on e1, supporting the e-pawn and preparing for more active central play.
Black plays d6, reinforces the e5 pawn and builds a compact central structure.
White plays c3, giving the centre extra support and preparing to expand with the d-pawn.
Black develops the bishop to e6, improving piece activity and challenging White's active bishop.
White retreats the bishop to b3, keeping it active while preserving the pressure along the diagonal.
Black plays h6, giving the king side some breathing room and asking White's pieces to stay alert.
White finally pushes d4, taking more space in the centre and increasing the tension.
Black exchanges in the centre with exd4, trying to reduce White's space and activity.
White recaptures with the c-pawn, rebuilding a strong central pawn presence.
Black places the rook on e8. The pieces are now arranged in a way that gives White a tactical opportunity on the very next move.

hints: Look for one piece that can attack two targets at the same time.
Focus on White's central pawn.
Can the pawn advance while attacking two pieces?
Look carefully at the d5 square.
lessons.takeaway: A central pawn can become a powerful tactical weapon when advancing it attacks two pieces at once.
